A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QLIP work. The complete main texts, equations, six tables, nineteen figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaVA-QLIP benchmark evaluations, interpolation experiments, pruning ablations, and training analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons and detailed appendix sweeps.

M1.justification: The quadtree selection procedure, coordinate-based MLP, Fourier features, combined training loss, and inference procedure are retained. Revised descriptions of CLIP and training requirements do not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Imagenette and evaluate V*, MM-Bench, POPE, CV-Bench, visual ScienceQA, MME, and RealWorld-QA. Newly discussed domains and encoder families are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The LLaVA-1.5 baselines, S² and SEAL literature comparisons, bilinear/bicubic interpolation controls, and random-pruning comparisons retain the same membership. Discussion of newer encoders adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported training settings, model sizes, metrics, cropping procedures, and resolution/alpha sweeps are unchanged. v2's recommendations for choosing alpha are usage guidance rather than a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The interpolation ablations, derivative-versus-random pruning comparisons, resolution sensitivity plots, and training hyperparameter analyses are retained. The detailed appendix analyses are relocated without additional tests.

E5.justification: Figure 7 still reports ten random-selection runs with averages, standard deviations, and min/max shading. Figures 18–19 still specify single random-selection trials. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the plotted experimental results are unchanged, including all 1,044 appendix sweep scores. Table 1 retains V* accuracies of 53.4 and 58.6 for QLIP-7B and QLIP-13B. New explanatory discussion supplies no additional measured outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the explicit global-average-pooling characterization of the CLIP CLS token and instead invokes transformer pooling in the argument motivating the residual loss. This is a limited revision to the mathematical rationale; the sum-based invariance argument and equations (1)–(5) remain unchanged, without a new proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the two identified biases, quadtree patchification, learned positional interpolation, and improved VQA with frozen backbone weights. Naming the vision encoder and LLM explicitly in the no-retraining claim clarifies a distinction already supported by v1's disclosed MLP training.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit exclusions for dense prediction, lack of validation on non-natural images, and compatibility limits for newer encoders. Section 4 discusses attenuation of coarse cues and existing general-VQA regressions, while removing v1's ScienceQA CLS-dependence speculation. The original limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Appendix H reports training and evaluation code as available, whereas v1 Appendix G planned its release. v2 also adds MLP-reuse, alpha-tuning, and inference-overhead guidance. Model weights and the single reproduction command remain described prospectively.

R1.justification: The cited works are retained, but Section 6 adds positioning against newer encoders such as InternVL and Qwen-V and explicitly distinguishes pre-encoding patchification from post-encoding token pruning. The QWEN integration discussion already existed in v1's appendix.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits and selectively rewrites explanatory paragraphs, changes citation style, moves Limitations to Appendix A, and adds acknowledgements and an LLM-use statement. The main section sequence and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is restyled, Figure 1 moves onto the first page, and several figures and tables are resized or regrouped. Figure 4's caption correctly identifies cosine similarity in the first panel and interpolation bias in the middle panel. The underlying displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through clearer training scope, more explicit applicability limits, and discussion of existing regressions. It also corrects Figure 4's misleading panel descriptions and reports code availability. These are useful, limited improvements; the empirical evidence remains unchanged, and weights and complete reproduction instructions remain partly prospective.
